title: Locating an earthquake from the S–P delay
caption: P waves (about 6 km s⁻¹) outrun S waves (about 3.4 km s⁻¹), so the gap between their arrivals grows with distance: about 1 s for every 8 km. An S wave 30 s behind the P wave puts the quake about 240 km away; three stations fix the epicentre.
alt: Arrival time against distance for P and S waves, two straight lines from the origin that spread apart, with a 30 second gap at 240 kilometres marked.
description: P arrival: t = d / 6. S arrival: t = d / 3.43.
The gap grows as d (1/v_S − 1/v_P) = d / 8 s per km.
A 30 s gap: d = 8 × 30 = 240 km (P at 40 s, S at 70 s).

checks.name: the gap grows 1 s per 8 km
